Test: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A proof list names a test that is not on the branch. The log reports the missing test but tells the user to run `forge close` without first correcting the proof or adding the test. Closing does not repair the proof; when it reaches the failed check, it instead directs the user to `forge work` (`src/forge/close.py:477`, `src/forge/checks.py:27`). The advertised next step therefore cannot clear this refusal and leads through another close round.
findings.title: Not done: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A proof list contains more than one missing test, or has no test mapping and produces both a refusal and its repair instruction. The named test creates and checks only one reason, and it asserts the ineffective `forge close` next step. `proof.check` can return multiple messages (`src/forge/proof.py:203` and `src/forge/proof.py:218`), so an implementation that logs only the first reason would still pass this test. The test should check all reasons and an actionable next step for a failed check.
findings.title: Test: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.

why: When forge-pr-check fails on GitHub, the job log printed by the Report review status step is empty, so the real reason is hidden and close suggests a new build round (issue #1803).
